solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Platform favourite entertaining everyone

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, as in teacher's pet
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A favourite performer on a stage keeps the whole audience amused.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallet is a flat wooden platform for stacking and moving goods.

clue.text: Ace endowed with divine favour better than the rest

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
blest is an old spelling of blessed, favoured by God

explanation.surface: A star player blessed by heaven outdoes the others.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of able means most capable, so superior to all others.

clue.text: Workers in party beneficial to Anglican church

parts.note: Labour is a British political party
something beneficial to you is for you
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Members of a political party who favour the established church.
explanation.definitionFit: The workforce is the body of people employed or available for work.

clue.text: Bridged river to the north, having installed some lines?

indicators.note: installed means put inside, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue, going north means reading the river's name upwards, from the end

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
a verse is a few lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A river was spanned up north, with some lines of a poem fitted in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to the north' means read upwards; the Dart is a river in Devon. 'Bridged' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross from side to side, as a bridge spans a gap.

clue.text: Slur that brings two characters together

definitions.meaning: in music a slur, the curved line joining notes, is also called by this name
in printing, two letters such as f and i joined into one glyph form this

explanation.surface: An insult that unites two people in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is both a musical slur and a typographic joining of two letters into one character.

clue.text: Deficient character? Could include a daughter!

definitions.text: Deficient character? Could include a daughter!

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the other pieces inside it
deficient means lacking, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a character in writing is a letter

explanation.surface: A worried parent fears that a badly behaved character might turn out to be their own daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deficient' cuts LETTER to LETTE, and 'Could include' puts A and D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman given to loud, boozy, laddish behaviour, a character some would call lacking.

clue.text: Express horror about king getting total possession

indicators.note: about means around, so the gasp goes round the other piece

parts.note: to gasp is to express horror or shock
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: People react in shock when a monarch seizes absolute control.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something in your hold or full control is the noun sense here.

clue.text: A "mini-mountain" of rubbish piled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, piled up means built upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A little hill formed by a heap of garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor, smaller than a true peak.

clue.text: Reluctant to talk when name is brought up in rift

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rift

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised, read from the bottom

parts.note: to name, as in quoting a source, is to cite

explanation.surface: Someone won't speak once a person is mentioned during a falling-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name' is a verb here, as in naming a source, not a noun abbreviated to N.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticent means reserved, not revealing one's thoughts readily.

clue.text: Inadequate sign at entrance to dull entertainment zone

indicators.note: placed at the entrance of the next piece, so it comes first
inadequate means falling short, so the word for a sign loses its final letter

parts.note: a sign or indication is a clue
dull means bland

explanation.surface: A poor notice at the door of a boring nightspot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' tempts as a card-suit club; it is a clue, docked of its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubland is the district of a city full of nightclubs, an area of nightlife and amusement.

clue.text: First of Tia Maria's done for a divine drink!

indicators.note: done in the sense of done in, ruined, so the letters are knocked into a new order
only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A drinker has polished off a glass of Tia Maria, the coffee liqueur, and toasts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' signals an anagram of T (first of Tia) plus MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu myth amrita is the nectar of immortality drunk by the gods, a drink of the divine.

clue.text: Don's conjecture

definitions.meaning: to don clothes is to put them on, take on
to conjecture is to suppose or take for granted

explanation.surface: A university teacher's theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a name or an Oxford tutor; here it is the verb meaning put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both put on (a garment or air) and suppose are senses of this verb.

clue.text: Sort to confront Roman maybe

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type
to confront is to face

explanation.surface: A kind of person squares up to a citizen of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' is the printing style, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman, upright printing letters, is one example of a font style.

clue.text: One exemplifies it formally

parts.note: the formal pronoun one, as in one does one's best, stands for the speaker themself, so it is an instance of this grammatical category

explanation.surface: A single example illustrates a point in a formal way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like the number; it is the posh pronoun meaning I.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, the speaker's own pronouns, I and the formal one, belong to this category.

clue.text: Childminder sent for pater when in difficulty

indicators.note: letters in difficulty are in a mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A babysitter is called in to look after the children while father struggles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises a child not their own is one kind of carer for children.

clue.text: Priest initially getting to a particular clerical activity

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter is used

parts.note: getting to a place is reaching it

explanation.surface: A priest begins to arrive at some churchly duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering sermons is a central task for clergy.

clue.text: Fairy nothing other than heartless, a mischievous little thing

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: nothing other than means sheer, as in sheer nonsense

explanation.surface: A fairy, simply cruel, is a naughty little sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the central E of SHEER to leave SHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Perisher is British slang for an annoying or naughty child, a little rascal.

clue.text: Playing field has offensive smell coming back again

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field
offensive means rude
a smell is a scent

explanation.surface: The local sports ground once again reeks of something nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Recrudescent describes something, such as a disease, breaking out again after dormancy.

clue.text: Perfect and totally dull — one bound for university!

indicators.note: one letter is bound for, taking the place of, the other

parts.note: a sunless day is totally dull, with no sun at all
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A flawless but utterly boring student heads off to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound for' means I goes in place of U in SUNLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of all wrongdoing means morally faultless.

clue.text: A funny person finishing early with extremely operatic piece?

indicators.note: the word ends early, losing its final letter

parts.note: a very funny person is a riot
extremely means so, as in so good

explanation.surface: A comedian cuts short a highly operatic number.
explanation.definitionFit: An arioso is a vocal passage in opera between recitative and a full aria.

clue.text: Very elaborate punishments — a joke

parts.note: fines are monetary punishments
a pun is a joke made on words

explanation.surface: Penalties so ornate they seem a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Finespun means drawn out very thin, hence delicate, overly intricate or subtle.

clue.text: Quiet island in critically difficult time

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
an inch is a small island, a Scottish word

explanation.surface: A peaceful island during a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; INCH is a Scottish term for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch, a crisis or emergency moment, is the idiom.

clue.text: An expression of emotion when that lady's in red

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cry expresses emotion
that lady is her

explanation.surface: A woman dressed in red sobs with feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is a bright red shade, the colour of the fruit.

clue.text: Girl mostly difficult for boy to catch

indicators.note: the boy's word catches and holds the other piece within

parts.note: a boy is a son

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: difficult means hard

explanation.surface: A girl finds a boy hard to win over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharon is a female given name.

clue.text: Whiskey or port?

definitions.meaning: a North American whiskey distilled from this grain
a town in East Sussex, one of the old Cinque Ports

explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine; it is the harbour town of Rye in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye whiskey is a spirit, and Rye is a historic English harbour town.

clue.text: Harmful substance to be limited? Europe's prime task

indicators.note: the prime, or first, letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a task is a mission

explanation.surface: European policymakers set curbing a dangerous substance as their main job.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollutant discharges, such as carbon dioxide from exhausts, are things governments aim to cap.

clue.text: Riding attire splits audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so a word sounding the same is meant

parts.note: splits or ruptures are breaches

explanation.surface: Riding trousers tear with a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeches are short trousers fastened below the knee, worn for horse riding.

clue.text: Advanced travel needing gas

parts.note: to travel is to go
neon is a noble gas

explanation.surface: Progress on a journey requiring fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: To have moved forward or continued is a phrasal idiom for having advanced.
